--- title: "[Duration]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} A time argument computed as the elapsed time between two date or datetime columns. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_ingest.py#L68-L149){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python Duration(start, end, unit="days") ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A `Duration` is a frozen specification that names two date or datetime columns and a time unit. When passed to an `Outcome` constructor as the `time` (or `time2`) argument, Greenwood computes the elapsed time automatically when the data is read. Inside a formula, write the same thing as `duration(start, end, unit="days")`. Create a `Duration` with the `duration()` helper rather than constructing it directly. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [start]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Column name holding the origin date or datetime (e.g., enrollment date). [end]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Column name holding the exit date or datetime (e.g., date of event or last contact). [unit]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["days"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Time unit for the elapsed duration: `"days"` (default), `"weeks"`, `"months"`, `"years"`, `"hours"`, `"minutes"`, or `"seconds"`. Months and years use average Gregorian lengths (30.4375 and 365.25 days). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Create a `Duration` that computes follow-up time in days between two date columns, and use it as the time argument of an `Outcome`: ::: {#03ea9ab6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw import polars as pl df = pl.DataFrame({ "enroll": ["2020-01-01", "2020-03-15", "2020-06-01"], "last_contact": ["2021-06-15", "2020-12-01", "2022-01-10"], "event": [1, 0, 1], }).with_columns( pl.col("enroll").str.to_date(), pl.col("last_contact").str.to_date(), ) d = gw.duration(start="enroll", end="last_contact", unit="days") d ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` duration(start='enroll', end='last_contact', unit='days') ``` ::: ::: ::: {#e1b578df .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} y = gw.Outcome.surv(time=d, event="event").bind(df) y ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` Surv(type=right, n=3, events=2) ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
columns The two columns the duration reads.
### [columns]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} The two columns the duration reads. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [columns]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[str, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
compute() The elapsed time from `start` to `end` in `unit` (`NaN` where either is missing).
### [compute()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} The elapsed time from `start` to `end` in `unit` (`NaN` where either is missing). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_ingest.py#L134-L146){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python compute(start, end) ``` :::
